sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. I am Emili. Today we will talk about
Stavanger. Stavanger is a city in Norway. It is in the southwest part of the country
near the sea. Stavanger is a small and beautiful city. It is famous for its old wooden houses,
oil industry, and natural beauty. The city is quiet and clean. People love to walk by the harbor
and enjoy the fresh air. Let's learn more about this lovely city by the sea. Part 2.
Where is Stavanger? Stavanger is on the west coast of Norway. It is next to the north sea.
It is not a very big city but it is very important for Norway. Many people call it
the oil capital of Norway. The city is surrounded by mountains, green hills, and water. You can see
boats everywhere, big ships, small fishing boats, and ferries. The air is cool and fresh
and the city looks beautiful in every season. Part 3. A Short History of Stavanger.
Stavanger is an old city. It became a town in the year 1125 when the Stavanger Cathedral was built.
In the past, people in Stavanger worked as fishermen. The city was famous for fishing and
making canned fish. Later, in the 1960s, oil was found in the north sea. This changed everything.
Stavanger became rich and modern. Today, Stavanger is a mix of old and new,
old houses, modern offices, and a strong economy. Part 4. The Old Town.
Gumbelstavanger. One of the most beautiful parts of the city is Gumbelstavanger, which means old
Stavanger. It has more than 170 white wooden houses from the 18th and 19th centuries. The streets
are small, clean, and full of flowers. People love to walk there, take photos, and enjoy the
quiet. It feels like going back in time. This area is one of the best preserved old towns in Europe.
Part 5. Stavanger Cathedral. The Stavanger Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in Norway.
It was built almost 900 years ago. It is in the center of the city near the lake.
The building is made of stone and has beautiful windows and carvings. Many people visit it
every year to see its history and art. It is still used today for church services,
weddings, and concerts. The cathedral is a symbol of Stavanger's long and proud history.
Part 6. The Oil City Stavanger is called the Oil Capital of Norway. When oil was discovered in the
North Sea, Stavanger became the center of Norway's oil industry. Many people came to work here from
other countries. Today, the city has many companies that work with oil and energy. There is even a
Norwegian Petroleum Museum where visitors can learn about oil and how it changed Norway.
Oil made Stavanger modern and international. Part 7. Nature Around Stavanger. Nature Around Stavanger
is amazing. You can see green hills, blue fjords, and tall mountains. One of the most famous
places near the city is Pryka Stolen, also called Pulpit Rock. It is a high cliff
with an incredible view of the fjord below. People from all over the world come to hike there.
It takes about two hours to walk to the top and the view is worth it. There are also beaches,
forests, and lakes near Stavanger for people who love nature. Part 8. Weather and Stavanger.
Stavanger has cool and mild weather. It rains a lot because it is near the sea. Winter is cold
and windy but not too snowy. Spring and summer are beautiful. The days are long and the sun shines
until late at night. People like to spend time outside when it's sunny, walking, cycling,
or sitting by the harbor with ice cream. Even when it rains, Stavanger feels peaceful and cozy.
Part 9. Food and Stavanger. Food and Stavanger is delicious and fresh. People eat a lot of fish,
salmon, cod, and shrimp. One famous dish is Fiskasupa, a creamy fish soup with vegetables.
There are also many international restaurants because people from many countries live here.
If you visit the harbor, you can find food trucks and cafes with local snacks. And of course,
Norwegians love coffee. They drink it all day. Part 10. Festivals and Culture.
Stavanger has many festivals and cultural events. One of the biggest is the Gladmat Festival,
a food festival every summer. People cook, taste, and celebrate food from all over the world.
There is also the Stavanger International Jazz Festival, called May Jazz, where musicians come
from many countries. Street art is very popular too. You can see colorful murals on buildings all
around the city. Art, music, and food make Stavanger full of life and color. Part 11.
People of Stavanger. People in Stavanger are friendly and polite. Many of them speak very good
English. Family and outdoor life are very important. People love hiking, sailing, and spending weekends
in nature. Stavanger is also an international city. You can hear many languages on the streets,
English, Polish, Spanish, and more. The mix of cultures makes the city open and warm.
I am Emili. Stavanger is a small city with a big heart. It has history, nature, and a modern spirit.
You can walk through old white houses, see the sea, eat fish soup, and enjoy the quiet beauty
of Norway. It is a city where the past meets the future. Old streets and new ideas, peace and
progress. I hope you can visit Stavanger one day and feel its calm and charm. Goodbye. Or as they
say in Norwegian. Adabra!
